query: An FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy-alloy bond coat deposited from 15–45 μm feedstock does not attain the required coating thickness. For thermal-spray deposition and subsequent service as a bond coat in a thermal barrier coating system, what single intervention could overcome this thickness shortfall while preserving coating integrity and minimal as-sprayed oxidation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, the operating and service conditions under which it should remain effective, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Shifting the feedstock particle size distribution upward (e.g., from 15–45 μm to a distribution with a higher minimum and maximum, such as ~30–75 μm) will enable the deposition of a thicker FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy-alloy bond coat while preserving coating integrity and limiting oxidation during thermal-spray processing.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy-alloy bond coat deposited from 15–45 μm feedstock that currently results in insufficient coating thickness.
generation.intervention: Use a modified feedstock with a larger particle size distribution (~30–75 μm) during thermal-spray deposition.
generation.conditions: Thermal-spray deposition carried out under standard inert or low-oxygen conditions and followed by service as a bond coat in a thermal barrier coating system.
generation.structural_mediator: Increased particle size leads to larger molten droplets that produce thicker splats upon impact, reducing the number of interfaces and thereby improving overall coating build-up while still mitigating oxidation because processing parameters (e.g., inert atmosphere) remain unchanged.
generation.mechanism: Larger particles have higher momentum and can form thicker splats that adhere more effectively, resulting in an overall thicker deposit. The maintained inert or low-oxygen environment during deposition prevents excessive oxidation despite the higher energy input and larger particle sizes.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline 15–45 μm feedstock deposit, the engineered larger particle feedstock is expected to yield a significantly thicker coating, with an increase of at least 20% in thickness, while achieving comparable levels of as-sprayed oxidation and coating microstructural integrity.
generation.baseline: Coatings produced using 15–45 μm feedstock have a thickness shortfall under identical thermal-spray conditions.
generation.boundary: The intervention should remain effective under typical thermal-spray deposition conditions (with controlled atmosphere and optimized particle acceleration) and subsequent service conditions encountered in thermal barrier coating systems. Extreme deviations in process parameters or environmental oxygen levels might compromise the benefits.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty exists regarding the optimal particle size range to achieve the target thickness without inadvertently increasing oxidation or compromising the coating’s mechanical properties. There is also some uncertainty on whether larger particles may affect splat adhesion or introduce novel defects.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of deposits under identical thermal-spray conditions: one using the baseline 15–45 μm feedstock and another using the modified larger particle feedstock (e.g., ~30–75 μm). Both sets should be sprayed under the same inert atmosphere and processing parameters. Post-deposition, measure coating thickness, microstructural integrity (using electron microscopy), and quantify oxide content (using X-ray diffraction or similar spectroscopy methods).
measurements: Oxide content/phase formation (via XRD or similar technique)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the modified feedstock does not result in a coating that is at least 20% thicker than the baseline without increasing the oxidation level by more than approximately 5% relative to the baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified.
